name.text: Intersecting chords - find the missing segment (INNODEMS)

questiontext.text:
In the figure, the chords \(AB\) and \(CD\) of the circle intersect at \(P\). You are given

\[ AP = {@AP@}\text{ cm}, \qquad PB = {@PB@}\text{ cm}, \qquad CP = {@CP@}\text{ cm}, \]

and the length \(PD = x\) cm is unknown. Find \(PD\).

[[jsxgraph width="470px" height="470px"]] var AP = {#AP#}, PB = {#PB#}, CP = {#CP#}, PD = {#PD#}; var rad = Math.PI / 180; var aAB = 20 * rad; var aCD = 75 * rad; var ux = Math.cos(aAB), uy = Math.sin(aAB); var vx = Math.cos(aCD), vy = Math.sin(aCD); var Ap = [-AP * ux, -AP * uy]; var Bp = [ PB * ux, PB * uy]; var Cp = [-CP * vx, -CP * vy]; var Dp = [ PD * vx, PD * vy]; function circum(p1, p2, p3) { var x1 = p1[0], y1 = p1[1], x2 = p2[0], y2 = p2[1], x3 = p3[0], y3 = p3[1]; var d = 2 * (x1 * (y2 - y3) + x2 * (y3 - y1) + x3 * (y1 - y2)); var cx = ((x1*x1 + y1*y1) * (y2 - y3) + (x2*x2 + y2*y2) * (y3 - y1) + (x3*x3 + y3*y3) * (y1 - y2)) / d; var cy = ((x1*x1 + y1*y1) * (x3 - x2) + (x2*x2 + y2*y2) * (x1 - x3) + (x3*x3 + y3*y3) * (x2 - x1)) / d; return [cx, cy]; } var ctr = circum(Ap, Bp, Cp); var rr = Math.hypot(ctr[0] - Ap[0], ctr[1] - Ap[1]); var pad = 1.6; var board = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard(divid, { boundingbox: [ctr[0] - rr - pad, ctr[1] + rr + pad, ctr[0] + rr + pad, ctr[1] - rr - pad], keepaspectratio: true, axis: false, showCopyright: false, showNavigation: false }); board.create('circle', [ctr, rr], {strokeColor: '#888', strokeWidth: 1.5, fixed: true}); var A = board.create('point', Ap, {name: 'A', size: 2, fixed: true, fillColor: '#333', strokeColor: '#333', label: {offset: [-12, -2], anchorX: 'right', anchorY: 'middle'}}); var B = board.create('point', Bp, {name: 'B', size: 2, fixed: true, fillColor: '#333', strokeColor: '#333', label: {offset: [10, 8], anchorX: 'left', anchorY: 'bottom'}}); var C = board.create('point', Cp, {name: 'C', size: 2, fixed: true, fillColor: '#333', strokeColor: '#333', label: {offset: [-10, -8], anchorX: 'right', anchorY: 'top'}}); var D = board.create('point', Dp, {name: 'D', size: 2, fixed: true, fillColor: '#333', strokeColor: '#333', label: {offset: [0, 12], anchorX: 'middle', anchorY: 'bottom'}}); var P = board.create('point', [0, 0], {name: 'P', size: 2, fixed: true, fillColor: '#333', strokeColor: '#333', label: {offset: [9, -4], anchorX: 'left', anchorY: 'top'}}); board.create('segment', [A, B], {strokeColor: '#1565c0', strokeWidth: 2.5, fixed: true}); board.create('segment', [C, D], {strokeColor: '#d32f2f', strokeWidth: 2.5, fixed: true}); var nAB = [-uy, ux], nCD = [-vy, vx], off = 0.55; function lbl(p1, p2, n, sgn, txt) { board.create('text', [(p1[0] + p2[0]) / 2 + sgn * off * n[0], (p1[1] + p2[1]) / 2 + sgn * off * n[1], txt], {anchorX: 'middle', anchorY: 'middle', fontSize: 13, fixed: true, cssStyle: 'color:#333'}); } lbl(Ap, [0, 0], nAB, 1, AP + ' cm'); lbl([0, 0], Bp, nAB, -1, PB + ' cm'); lbl(Cp, [0, 0], nCD, 1, CP + ' cm'); lbl([0, 0], Dp, nCD, 1, 'x cm'); [[/jsxgraph]]
\( PD = \) [[input:ans1]]\(\text{ cm}\) [[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]

generalfeedback.text:
When two chords intersect inside a circle, the product of the two parts of one chord equals the product of the two parts of the other:

\[ AP \cdot PB = CP \cdot PD. \]

Substituting the given lengths,

\[ {@AP@} \cdot {@PB@} = {@CP@} \cdot PD \;\;\Longrightarrow\;\; PD = \frac{{@AP@} \cdot {@PB@}}{{@CP@}} = \frac{{@AP*PB@}}{{@CP@}} = {@ta1@}. \]

So \(PD = {@ta1@}\) cm.

node.description: Additive slip: used AP + PB = CP + PD.

truefeedback.text: It looks like you combined the lengths by adding. For two chords meeting inside a circle it is the products of the two parts that are equal, not the sums. Set up \( AP\cdot PB = CP\cdot PD \) and try again.

node.description: Mispairing AP*PD = CP*PB (paired AP with PD).

truefeedback.text: It looks like you set \( AP\cdot PD = CP\cdot PB \), pairing \(AP\) with \(PD\). But each product should multiply the two parts of the same chord: \( AP\cdot PB \) for chord \(AB\), and \( CP\cdot PD \) for chord \(CD\). Set those equal and try again.

node.description: Mispairing AP*CP = PD*PB (paired AP with CP).

truefeedback.text: It looks like you set \( AP\cdot CP = PD\cdot PB \), pairing \(AP\) with \(CP\) — but those are parts of different chords. Use \( AP\cdot PB \) for chord \(AB\) and \( CP\cdot PD \) for chord \(CD\), then solve.

falsefeedback.text: Not correct. Use the intersecting-chords relationship: the product of the two parts of one chord equals the product of the two parts of the other. Form an equation in \(PD\) and solve it. Have another go.
